exposure: Decabrominated diphenyl ether (PBDE-209) intragastrically administered at doses of 1, 5, and 10 mg/kg b.w. daily during gestation
outcome: Placental mRNA and protein expression of ET-1
Placental mRNA and protein expression of eNOS
Placental mRNA and protein expression of iNOS
Total nitric oxide (NO) in the placenta
cohort: Pregnant Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were randomly divided into five groups (control, vehicle, and three PBDE-209 exposure groups).
finding: Maternal exposure to PBDE-209 during pregnancy significantly increased placental ET-1 and iNOS expression, decreased placental eNOS expression, increased total NO production, and reduced the birth weight of offspring rats.
birth_weight: Offspring birth weight was significantly reduced after maternal exposure to 5 and 10 mg/kg b.w. PBDE-209.
gest_age: Exposure occurred from day 0 (G0) to day 21 (G21) gestation, with placental samples collected on G21.
